source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 9: work done by a constant force (book p.275). Answer 56 Nm agrees with the key (PDF 312).

blocks.prompt: 9. Find the work done, if the point at which the constant force \(\underline{F} = 2\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\) is applied to an object, moves it from \(P_1(2, -3, 1)\) to \(P_2(7, 5, 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
A work-done question: one constant force and a straight displacement.
We must find the work \(W\) (a number).
Plan: find \(\underline{d} = \underline{P_1P_2}\), then \(W = \underline{F}\cdot\underline{d}\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{F} = 2\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\); the point moves from \(P_1(2, -3, 1)\) to \(P_2(7, 5, 3)\).
To find: work done \(W\).
Method: Work done by a constant force \(W = \underline{F}\cdot\underline{d}\) (14.2.8), where \(\underline{d}\) is the displacement vector from the starting point to the end point.

Displacement
\[\underline{d} = \underline{P_1P_2} = (7 - 2)\underline{i} + (5 + 3)\underline{j} + (3 - 1)\underline{k}\]
\[= 5\underline{i} + 8\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\]
Why: End point minus starting point.

Work done
\[W = (2\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 3\underline{k})\cdot(5\underline{i} + 8\underline{j} + 2\underline{k})\]
\[= 10 + 40 + 6 = 56\]
Why: Dot product of force and displacement.

Check
\[|\underline{F}| = \sqrt{38},\ |\underline{d}| = \sqrt{93}\]
\[|\underline{F}||\underline{d}| \approx 59.4 > 56\]
Why: \(W = |\underline{F}||\underline{d}|\cos\theta\) can never exceed \(|\underline{F}||\underline{d}|\); it is close to it because the force points almost along the motion.
